name: kensaku
description: Search inside documents, code, and even screenshots - instantly and locally. A free, open-source file launcher with OCR, semantic search, and MCP agent access.
readme_summary: Kensaku is a fast, local-first desktop search application built with Rust and Tauri. It allows users to quickly find files by name, content within documents and images (via OCR), and even by semantic meaning. It also integrates with AI agents through the MCP protocol, prioritizing user privacy as nothing leaves the local machine.
key_features: Filename search in milliseconds
Full-text search within documents (PDF, DOCX, EPUB, etc.)
OCR for text extraction from screenshots and images
Semantic search for finding files by meaning
Natural language queries (e.g., 'screenshots from last week')
Integration with AI agents via MCP
Fast, incremental indexing
Privacy-focused, local-first operation
Open-source (MIT license)
primary_use_case: To provide users with an extremely fast and comprehensive local file search tool that goes beyond filenames to search document content, image text, and semantic meaning, while maintaining user privacy and offering AI agent integration.
cover_image_prompt: A curious librarian standing in a vast, dimly lit library filled with countless books. Instead of traditional searching, the librarian holds a glowing magnifying glass that, when pointed at any book, instantly reveals its contents as floating, illuminated text and relevant images in the air around it. Some of the floating text originates from within scanned book pages and even from images depicted within the books. Subtle digital particles emanate from the magnifying glass, and a small, unobtrusive UI element resembling a search bar with highlighted keywords hovers near the librarian's hand. The overall mood is one of effortless discovery and deep understanding. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a warm, inviting color palette and soft lighting, emphasizing the magic of instant knowledge retrieval.

name: fmx
description: Lightweight, fast media converter (video, audio, image, PDF) in Rust with an egui GUI
readme_summary: FMX is a free, open-source media converter built with Rust, offering a user-friendly egui GUI for converting various file types including video, audio, images, documents, and discs. It supports batch processing, system-wide integration via right-click context menus, and provides presets for popular devices and platforms.
key_features: All-in-one media conversion (video, audio, image, PDF, eBooks, discs)
Lightweight and fast performance
Simple and intuitive egui GUI
Batch processing and queue management
Right-click integration with file manager
Presets for phones, devices, and platforms (e.g., iPhone, Android, YouTube)
Editing features (trim, crop, rotate, subtitles)
Supports a wide range of input and output formats
Free, open-source, no ads, no account required
primary_use_case: To provide a simple, fast, and versatile desktop application for converting various media file types without requiring users to install multiple specialized tools.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic toolbox labeled 'FMX' standing in a bright, organized workshop. The toolbox is actively sorting and transforming a stream of diverse media icons (video cameras, music notes, image files, document pages, discs) into neat stacks of universally recognized output icons (like a play button for video, headphones for audio, a picture frame for images). Subtle digital particles flow from the input stream to the output stacks. In the background, a small, clean monitor displays a progress bar and the FMX logo. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a vibrant, inviting color palette.

name: ffmpeg-skill
description: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.
readme_summary: ffmpeg-skill provides a local, offline video editing environment for AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor. It offers 42 FFmpeg-based tools accessible via a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, enabling agents to perform tasks such as cutting, adding captions, reframing, and loudness normalization without relying on cloud services or API keys.
key_features: 42 FFmpeg tools for video editing (cut, captions, reframe, loudness, etc.)
Machine-readable contract and MCP server for agent integration
Local, offline operation (no cloud, no API keys)
Python standard library compatibility
Automatic generation of tool input schemas from argparse
Support for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients
Fixed workflow: probe -> edit -> check -> verify
Tested FFmpeg compatibility (6.1, 7.1, 8, 9)
primary_use_case: To empower AI coding agents with a comprehensive, local video editing capability, allowing them to process and manipulate video files directly without external dependencies or data uploads.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan, depicted as a friendly robot with a digital interface on its chest, meticulously crafting a film reel. The robot is shown taking raw, unedited footage (represented by tangled film strips) and precisely cutting, splicing, and adding vibrant subtitles (glowing text elements) to create a polished movie reel. Small, holographic screens around the robot display FFmpeg commands and visual waveforms, subtly indicating the underlying technology. The background is a clean, organized workshop with a hint of code flowing like digital dust. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a bright, approachable color palette, emphasizing precision and creative transformation.

name: Google-Maps-Scrapper
description: This code is used to perform web scraping and data extraction from Google Maps. It is particularly designed for obtaining information about businesses, including their name, address, website, phone number, reviews, and more.
readme_summary: This Python repository uses Playwright to scrape business information from Google Maps, extracting details like name, address, website, reviews, and operating hours. It cleans the data and exports it to a CSV file for further analysis.
key_features: Data Scraping from Google Maps listings
Extraction of business name, address, website, contact details
Scraping of review counts and average ratings
Detection of business services (in-store shopping, pickup, delivery)
Extraction of operating hours and introductory information
Data cleansing and organization
Export of cleaned data to CSV format
primary_use_case: Automated extraction of business information from Google Maps for analysis and integration into other applications.
cover_image_prompt: A digital cartographer meticulously drawing a detailed map of a bustling city, but instead of drawing lines, they are extracting glowing icons representing businesses. Each icon contains snippets of information like star ratings and phone numbers. The cartographer is using a magical magnifying glass that reveals the hidden data within the city's digital landscape. Subtle UI elements and data streams flow around them, hinting at the automated nature of the process. The overall scene is vibrant and informative, rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with a focus on clarity and a modern color palette.

name: portracker
description: An open source, self-hosted, real-time port monitoring and discovery tool.
readme_summary: Portracker is an open-source, self-hosted tool that automatically discovers and monitors network ports and services on your systems. It provides a real-time, visual map of your network, helping to prevent deployment issues and eliminate manual tracking.
key_features: Automatic Port Discovery
Platform-Specific Collectors (Docker, TrueNAS)
Internal Port Detection
Lightweight & Self-Contained (SQLite)
Peer-to-Peer Monitoring
Hierarchical Grouping
Enhanced TrueNAS Discovery
Modern & Responsive UI
primary_use_case: Real-time network port monitoring and service discovery for self-hosted environments.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant network cartographer standing at a crossroads, holding a magical spyglass that reveals glowing lines connecting various devices and services. The spyglass projects a live, dynamic map of interconnected ports and running services onto a large parchment. Small, subtle UI elements showing port numbers and service names float around the map. The scene is set in a cozy, dimly lit study filled with old maps and modern screens, with a gentle, ethereal glow emanating from the spyglass. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear iconography and a warm, inviting color palette, subtly incorporating the 'portracker' name into a compass rose on the map.

name: browserytools
description: 152 free browser-based tools in 17 languages. Your files and text are processed in your browser — no uploads, no accounts, no ads. Image & on-device AI tools, PDF, converters, formatters, calculators, generators. Some AI tools download model weights on first use.
readme_summary: BrowseryTools is a collection of 152 free, browser-based utility tools built with Next.js and TypeScript. All file and text processing happens client-side, ensuring privacy with no uploads, accounts, or ads. It includes various tools like image manipulation, PDF converters, and on-device AI functionalities powered by Transformers.js.
key_features: 152+ browser-based tools
Client-side processing (no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking)
On-device AI tools (transcription, translation, summarization, image upscaling)
Image manipulation (background removal, compression, format conversion, color correction)
PDF tools
Format converters
AI model weights downloaded on first use (privacy-preserving)
Multi-language support (17 languages)
primary_use_case: To provide users with a private, convenient, and free suite of browser-based tools for everyday tasks like image editing, file conversion, and AI-powered content processing, all without requiring any uploads or account creation.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, open browser window acting as a magical portal. Inside the portal, various digital tools and icons (like a paintbrush, a gear, a document icon, and a stylized brain for AI) are actively processing and transforming user data represented by glowing particles and simple shapes. On one side of the portal, raw data (like an image file icon and text snippets) enters, and on the other side, refined outputs (like a perfectly edited image, a converted document, and summarized text) emerge. The scene is clean, bright, and inviting, with subtle code snippets and the 'BrowseryTools' logo integrated into the browser's UI. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a friendly, modern aesthetic.
